profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Postmates Inc.
profile.summary: Experienced Senior Software Engineer with a demonstrated history of working in the internet industry. Skilled in HTML, Solr, Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), MongoDB, and Python (Programming Language). Strong engineering professional with a Master of Arts (MA) focused in Computer Science from Wesleyan University.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
My first task as a member of the Risk Team in the Data Org at Postmates was to automate evidence submission for Stripe chargeback disputes. This was an abandoned manual process that would consume approximately 5 person-hours of an analyst's time per week. The company has saved approximately $26k per month on average since launch.

I have also spent a significant amount of time refactoring and improving Pegasus, our real-time fraud engine. This work includes optimizations to allow for the arbitrary addition of new graph edges between different entities involved in possibly fraudulent transactions, allowing us to form richer connections and graph-based models. A great deal of the refactoring was done to introduce additional structures and guardrails to facilitate ease of development on behalf of our data scientists. Adding composable risk factors to Pegasus enabled us to support a use case that resulted in a savings of over $80,000 within 4 months.

Most recently, I have worked on the Pegasus API to allow for synchronous interactions with our fraud engine. Our first use case is expected to save us somewhere around ~$100,000 per month.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
As a member of the Data/Infrastructure team, I rewrote our events service (replacing our old REST API written in Node.js/Express in Python3/Flask, as well as creating Thrift endpoints for internal use), increasing our throughput by more than 2x. I also rewrote our people/identity (end-user) web API (again, from Node/Express to Py3/Flask). One of my final projects was also rewriting our content ingestion service and defining a beautiful, strongly-typed schema for representing customer content and data sources for individual properties.

For over a year (May 2014 - September 2015), I was the only engineer focused on customer needs, effectively being on-call all the time to fix critical bugs affecting our system, as well as adding essential features to address customers’ business requirements and to enhance their experience (e.g., adding support for multiple email templates, fixing campaign scheduling, tracking unsubscribes/resubscribes). I personally onboarded nearly 40 customers, actualizing $1 million in annual recurring revenue within 5 months of starting. I've had to fix bugs and address issues across key components of our API, including rewriting our /persons endpoint (for customers’ end-user data)--crushing the average error rate from 0.249% to 0.0082%--and optimizing the /resources controller (for ingesting customer content), speeding up performance by 2x. I singlehandedly overhauled our API and existing databases to fix a previous mistake in the architecture with virtually no downtime. One or my proudest achievements is authoring a library to validate internal data structures (`validator`!!!), which has the best test coverage (100%) out of any Boomtrain code repository.

I was also a proud member of Boomtrain's Standardization Task Force during the period we were predominantly a Node shop.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Wrote software components to serialize and parse EDI X12 eligibility and claim status transactions to and from health insurance companies and medical claims clearinghouses, including Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Kansas/Kansas City, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, and Cigna.

In my capacity as a data engineer, I optimized business and provider lookups by denormalizing data in MongoDB, analyzed insurance claim data and compiled cost reports for the top 50 most common medical procedures in cities across the US, and designed and laid the groundwork for a cost prediction tool for procedures.

positions.title: Senior Data Pipeline Engineer
positions.description: Maintained MySQL schema and Django models representing normalized music metadata as new fields and relationships were added, and configured Solr schema and data import handlers to import and index this metadata from MySQL across several Solr indexes. Wrote and maintained a suite of automated tests to ensure that newly ingested metadata, as well as overridden metadata, was properly properly indexed in Solr. Developed and wrote unit tests for components enabling the Python web service API to query Solr.

positions.title: QA Analyst Intern
positions.description: Thoroughly tested, documented, and reported bugs found in front-end applications used by a community of over 57,000 users; tracked bugs and oversaw them to their resolution; updated and maintained relevant design documents.

positions.title: CS Dept Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Graded homework and facilitated lab help sessions.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description: Implemented a statistical machine translation system for Xhosa to English text.

positions.title: DMP Research Intern
positions.description: Explored the effect of the perception of movement to the attribution of intelligence of animated figures; edited motion curves in Maya for experimental animations; put on a motion capture suit (!!!) for creating aforementioned animations.
